clue.text: Once the vehicle for the back-seat driver

definitions.text: Once the vehicle for the back-seat driver

parts.words: Once the vehicle for the back-seat driver
parts.note: a horse-drawn cab of the past whose driver sat up high behind the passengers, so he really was a back-seat driver

explanation.surface: A jibe at someone who nags from the rear of a car, now consigned to history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back-seat driver' suggests a passenger who criticises the driving; here it is literal, as the cabman's perch was at the rear of this two-wheeled Victorian cab.
explanation.definitionFit: This two-wheeled Victorian cab had its driver's seat raised behind the passenger compartment.

clue.text: In the 4, Venus may appear a wreck

definitions.text: In the 4, Venus may appear a wreck

parts.words: In the 4, Venus may appear a wreck
parts.note: 4 is the dusk answer, when the planet shows as the evening star, and a Longfellow poem tells of a schooner of that star's name being wrecked

explanation.surface: At dusk the goddess of love may look a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wreck of the Hesperus is Longfellow's ballad; the evening star is the classical Greek name for Venus seen after sunset.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek name for the evening star, the planet Venus at dusk, and the ship in a famous shipwreck ballad.

clue.text: It may be an Arabic or Roman symbol

definitions.text: It may be an Arabic or Roman symbol

parts.words: It may be an Arabic or Roman symbol
parts.note: Arabic and Roman suggest peoples, but both describe systems of writing figures such as 7 or VII

explanation.surface: A remark on whether a sign comes from the Arab world or ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arabic or Roman' tempts toward alphabets or cultures; both are kinds of written figure for counting.
explanation.definitionFit: A written figure standing for a number, such as 4 or IV.

clue.text: Little likelihood of a catch at cover-point

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator doubts a fielder at cover-point will take a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover-point is a cricket fielding position on the off side, so a catch offered there is a chance on the off.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote possibility; in cricket, a catching opportunity on the off side of the field.

clue.text: The sort of sleep that is divine in Wagner

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of slumber a Wagner opera portrays as godly.
explanation.walkthrough: Wagner's opera Götterdämmerung translates as the dusk of the gods, so the time of day belongs to the divine there.
explanation.definitionFit: A light anaesthetic state once used in childbirth was called this sleep; Wagner's final Ring opera is the gods' dusk.

clue.text: Old person goes about slurping a cocktail at a time of revelry

indicators.note: goes about means the word for old person surrounds the rest

parts.note: wight is an archaic word for a person or creature
taken as written

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of slurping are mixed

explanation.surface: An elderly drinker loudly sipping a mixed drink at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The old word for a creature, as in Chaucer, is split open; 'cocktail' mixes the slurping letters into LPURGISN, and 'goes about' wraps the old person round A plus that mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The eve of May Day, when witches were said to hold wild gatherings, is a night of festivity in central Europe.

clue.text: Suitable line for a cow-catcher

parts.note: a cow-catcher is the fender on a train, but here it is a cowboy roping cattle with a looped rope

explanation.surface: Advice on the right track for a locomotive's front grille.
explanation.walkthrough: A cow-catcher is the guard on the front of an American locomotive, and 'line' suggests railway track; here it is a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope with a running noose used by cowboys to catch cattle.

clue.text: The importance of scientific discovery

explanation.surface: A comment on how much a scientific finding matters.
explanation.walkthrough: The falling-apple story makes Newton's discovery fit the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Seriousness or weight of a matter; the force Newton described pulling bodies together.

clue.text: One who may have a temporary occupation

definitions.text: One who may have a temporary occupation

parts.words: One who may have a temporary occupation
parts.note: occupation means living in a property rather than a job, and a renter holds it only for the lease

explanation.surface: Describing a person in a short-term job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occupation' suggests employment; it means occupying a home.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rents and lives in property owned by a landlord.

clue.text: Lacking purpose, number join in mutiny

indicators.note: in places the number and join pieces within the word for mutiny

parts.note: an uprising is a revolt, like a mutiny
to enter a club or contest is to join it

explanation.surface: Aimless, a crowd joins in a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'join' is a verb, not a noun, and 'in' marks the container: the number and the verb go in just after the first letter of the revolt word.
explanation.definitionFit: Without initiative, drive or ambition.

clue.text: House finished —- few left at this stage

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, a common British type of home joined to one neighbour
final means last, finished, with nothing to follow

explanation.surface: A house is completed while only a handful of people remain.
explanation.walkthrough: In a knockout competition, the round before the final leaves just four contenders, so 'few left' describes this stage.
explanation.definitionFit: In a knockout tournament this penultimate round has only four players or teams remaining.

clue.text: Watering place in the country

parts.note: a spa is a resort with mineral springs where people once went to take the waters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A resort with mineral springs located somewhere in the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A European nation on the Iberian peninsula.

clue.text: Handle the artisan finally made of baked clay

parts.note: an ear is a handle on a jug or cup
taken as written

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word artisan

explanation.surface: A craftsman's jug handle turns out to be fired pottery after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Pottery or vessels of fired earth are described with this adjective.

clue.text: More work, to the point of being impractical

definitions.text: More work, to the point of being impractical

parts.words: More work, to the point of being impractical
parts.note: Thomas More wrote a book about an ideal island state, and an adjective formed from its title means idealistic to the point of being unworkable

explanation.surface: Someone piling on extra tasks until the plan becomes unrealistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' looks like 'additional'; it is Sir Thomas More, whose 1516 book named an imaginary perfect society.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealistic schemes that could never work in practice are described with this word, from More's imagined commonwealth.

clue.text: Old rider returns to take part in national hunt season

indicators.note: returns tells us the letters taken are to be read backwards
to take part in means the letters are a part of the following words, running across them

explanation.surface: A veteran jockey comes back to compete in the jump-racing season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take part in' marks NALHU inside 'national hunt', and 'returns' reads it backwards. National Hunt is British racing over jumps, which makes the jockey reading natural.
explanation.definitionFit: A lancer in the old Polish, Prussian or Austrian cavalry was a horseman of this name.

clue.text: With this one could make lofty observations

definitions.text: With this one could make lofty observations

parts.words: With this one could make lofty observations
parts.note: a bird of prey spots its quarry from great heights, and keen human sight is named after its vision

explanation.surface: Something that would allow you to see things from a great height.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lofty observations' sounds like grand remarks; it means literally seeing from high up, as a soaring raptor does.
explanation.definitionFit: Exceptionally sharp sight is named after the vision of a large raptor that hunts from high above.

clue.text: Bizarre like the Way of the World?

definitions.text: like the Way of the World?

explanation.surface: A query whether Congreve's play is strange.
explanation.walkthrough: The Way of the World is Congreve's comedy, but here it is the planet's path round the sun, which is elliptical, not a perfect circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd or unconventional; an orbit off a true circle, as the earth's is, is called this.

clue.text: What Macbeth did to sleep, when done in

explanation.surface: A question about the Scottish king's nights once he was killed.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare a voice cries 'Macbeth does murder sleep'; 'done in' is slang for killed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's line has Macbeth killing sleep; to be done in is to be killed.

clue.text: Tackles producing tries

explanation.surface: Rugby tackles leading to scores, as in a match report.
explanation.walkthrough: The rugby picture of tackles and tries misleads: both words are verbs or nouns meaning efforts.
explanation.definitionFit: To tackle a job or to try it is to make an effort at it; the plural nouns are efforts too.

clue.text: Paint for putting on outside

explanation.surface: Instructions for paint to be applied to exterior surfaces.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses come from one phrase: the final layer of paint, and an overcoat worn outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: The final layer of paint applied; an overcoat worn over other clothes.

clue.text: Chapter four involved an Ionian island

indicators.note: involved means twisted up or entangled, so the letters of four are mixed

explanation.surface: A book's chapter four features a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' is the anagram signal and makes ORFU; a chapter heading suggests a book, but C is just the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: This Greek holiday island lies in the Ionian Sea off the north-west coast.

clue.text: Award fora class in the old violin

indicators.note: in puts the class word inside the instrument

parts.note: a rote is a medieval stringed instrument, an old relative of the fiddle
a set is a group or class, as in a school set

explanation.surface: A prize for a group of students in early fiddle playing.
explanation.walkthrough: The rote, or crwth, was a medieval bowed instrument; the rosette is the ribbon prize at shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon badge given as a prize, for example at a horse or dog show.

clue.text: A Northerner, one stuck in the Smoke unfortunately

indicators.note: stuck in means the letter for one is lodged inside the rest
unfortunately signals the word Smoke is in a bad way and rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone from the north trapped in London, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Smoke is British slang for London, a fair misdirection. 'unfortunately' rearranges SMOKE to ESKMO, and 'stuck in' lodges I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated term for an Inuit person of the Arctic, a native of the far north.

clue.text: Concession by the Queen for singers

parts.note: a sop is a small concession made to pacify someone
a rani is a Hindu queen, wife of a rajah

explanation.surface: A royal grants a favour to a group of vocalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Queen' here is not ER but RANI, an Indian queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian plural for women or boys with the highest vocal range in a choir.

clue.text: One way to separate the flock

definitions.text: One way to separate the flock

parts.words: One way to separate the flock
parts.note: flock is the congregation of a church, and a walkway down the middle divides the pews

explanation.surface: Advice on dividing a herd of sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flock' suggests sheep; it is the congregation, split into two banks of pews by the central walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage between rows of seats in a church.

clue.text: Iodine's broken up into the smallest possible amounts

indicators.note: broken up signals the letters of the word before are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A chemist explains that iodine has been split into its tiniest portions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken up' rearranges IODINES; the 's of 'Iodine's' supplies the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Converted into charged atoms or molecules, the minute particles of chemistry.

clue.text: Kids follow one to the pictures

indicators.note: follow places the word for kids after the letter for one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to kid is to deceive or con someone

explanation.surface: Children trailing after somebody on a trip to the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kids' looks like children; it is a verb, to fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious images or symbolic representations, such as painted saints in Orthodox churches.

clue.text: One who may succeed without effort

definitions.text: One who may succeed without effort

parts.words: One who may succeed without effort
parts.note: succeed is read as taking over an estate or title from someone dead, which needs no work

explanation.surface: A description of a person who achieves things effortlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeed' seems to mean achieve; it means follow on, receiving what someone leaves behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who receives property or a title on another's death is a successor in that sense.

clue.text: Override, as ton-up boys presumably do

explanation.surface: Motorcycle tearaways are said to overrule something.
explanation.walkthrough: Ton-up boys were 1960s British bikers who rode at a hundred miles an hour; read as weighing over a ton, they exceed others in weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevail over or count for more than something; heavy men tip the scales beyond others.

clue.text: Letter of credit covered by growth potential

indicators.note: covered by puts the credit letters inside the word for growth potential

parts.note: a seed holds the potential to grow into a plant
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A bank's documentary credit is backed by the promise of growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter of credit' looks like a banking term, but 'of' is a link and 'Letter' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, rambling written piece, such as a tedious epistle, is this kind of document.
